content: Choosing an implementation: ETFs, SMAs and direct indexing

ETFs typically carry a lower headline expense ratio than a separately managed account's manager fee, since an ETF spreads trading and management costs across all shareholders. A separately managed account's fee reflects individualized management of your specific account -- including the ability to harvest losses at the position level and to exclude specific holdings.

Historical outperformance of passive index exposure over active management has been persistent across many periods, though performance varies by asset class, time horizon and market regime. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

A separately managed account can realize losses at the individual position level throughout the year, which a pooled ETF structure cannot do for an individual investor. This tax-loss harvesting capability is most valuable in volatile markets and for investors in higher tax brackets.
